title: A Point on the Leg
statement: Triangle $ABC$ has $AB = AC$ and $\angle BAC = 40^\circ$. Point $D$ lies on side $AC$, with $D \ne C$, and $BD = BC$. Find $\angle ABD$, in degrees.
hints: Start with the two equal angles of triangle $ABC$.
Triangle $BCD$ is isosceles too, with $BD = BC$. Find its angles, then compare $\angle DBC$ with $\angle ABC$.
solution: The angles of triangle $ABC$ at $B$ and $C$ are both $70^\circ$. In triangle $BCD$, $BD = BC$, so $\angle BDC = \angle BCD = 70^\circ$ and $\angle DBC = 40^\circ$. Hence $\angle ABD = 70^\circ - 40^\circ = 30^\circ$.

solution_figures.alt: Isosceles triangle ABC with AB = AC and a 40 degree angle at A. Point D on side AC has BD = BC, with tick marks on BD and BC. The angles at B and C of triangle ABC are 70 degrees, angle DBC is 40 degrees, and the highlighted angle ABD is 30 degrees.
